microtheory.name: behavioral_psychology
microtheory.definition: Behaviourism — Pavlov, Watson, Skinner. Focus on observable stimulus-response relationships. Internal mental states bracketed as 'black box'. Empirical strength: precise prediction of behaviour change. Limitations: under-explains language, problem-solving, internal experience. Substrate analogue: the substrate's stimulus → FilterSpec → ActionSpec → outcome loop IS behaviourism; the substrate's broader cortex architecture extends beyond it.

concepts.name: classical_conditioning
concepts.definition: Pavlov 1897. Neutral stimulus paired with biologically-significant stimulus comes to elicit the same response. Bell + food → salivation to bell. Substrate analogue: substrate's covers_correction strengthening when Concept_A reliably co-occurs with Concept_B.

concepts.name: unconditioned_stimulus
concepts.definition: Pavlov. Stimulus naturally producing a response (food). Substrate analogue: substrate's seeded high-valence Concept.

concepts.name: conditioned_stimulus
concepts.definition: Pavlov. Previously-neutral stimulus that comes to elicit response after pairing. Substrate analogue: substrate's Concept that gains valence through co-firing with high-valence Concepts.

concepts.name: extinction_behavioural
concepts.definition: Conditioned response weakens when CS presented without US. NOT erasure — original learning preserved, new inhibition learned. Substrate analogue: substrate's covers_correction decay when correction stops firing.

concepts.name: spontaneous_recovery
concepts.definition: After extinction, conditioned response can return after a rest period. Shows extinction is inhibition, not erasure. Substrate analogue: substrate's Mt-state reversion to prior basin when current context fades.

concepts.name: stimulus_generalisation
concepts.definition: Conditioning to one stimulus transfers to similar stimuli. Substrate analogue: substrate's similar-concept activation via shared causal_influence edges.

concepts.name: stimulus_discrimination
concepts.definition: Conditioned response only to specific CS, not similar stimuli. Substrate analogue: substrate's discrimination-drive sharpening Mt boundaries.

concepts.name: rescorla_wagner_model
concepts.definition: 1972. Conditioning strength changes proportional to prediction error: ΔV = α(λ - V). Foundation of all modern conditioning theory. Substrate analogue: substrate's J update rule — Hebbian × prediction error.

concepts.name: blocking
concepts.definition: Kamin 1969. Once a CS reliably predicts US, a new CS paired with the same US doesn't become associated. Refutes contiguity theories. Substrate analogue: substrate's existing covering FilterSpec prevents new ones from learning the same target.

concepts.name: operant_conditioning
concepts.definition: Skinner 1938. Behaviour modified by its consequences. Reinforcement increases; punishment decreases. Substrate analogue: substrate's ActionSpec coverage update based on event-outcome.

concepts.name: positive_reinforcement
concepts.definition: Adding desirable consequence → behaviour increases. Substrate analogue: positive RPE signal strengthening ActionSpec dispatch.

concepts.name: negative_reinforcement
concepts.definition: Removing aversive consequence → behaviour increases. Often confused with punishment. Substrate analogue: ActionSpec that reduces frustration gets reinforced.

concepts.name: positive_punishment
concepts.definition: Adding aversive consequence → behaviour decreases. Substrate analogue: high negative ΔF following ActionSpec dispatch.

concepts.name: negative_punishment
concepts.definition: Removing desirable consequence → behaviour decreases. 'Time out'. Substrate analogue: withholding reward signal after ActionSpec dispatch.

concepts.name: schedule_of_reinforcement
concepts.definition: Skinner. Pattern of reinforcement delivery: fixed ratio, variable ratio, fixed interval, variable interval. Each produces distinctive response pattern. Substrate analogue: substrate's reward-pattern shapes ActionSpec habit strength.

concepts.name: variable_ratio_schedule
concepts.definition: Reinforcement after unpredictable number of responses. Produces highest, most persistent response rate. Why gambling is addictive. Substrate analogue: high-variance-coverage ActionSpec — persistent dispatch.

concepts.name: shaping
concepts.definition: Skinner. Reinforce successive approximations to target behaviour. How animals learn complex tricks. Substrate analogue: substrate's correction-firing on increasingly-correct partial states.

concepts.name: chaining
concepts.definition: Linking simple behaviours into complex sequences. Each step's completion signals the next. Substrate analogue: substrate's FilterSpec → ActionSpec → next-FilterSpec dispatch chain.

concepts.name: premack_principle
concepts.definition: 1965. High-frequency behaviour can reinforce low-frequency behaviour. 'Eat your vegetables, then you can have dessert.' Substrate analogue: substrate's preferred-Mt access used to reinforce engagement with less-preferred Mt.

concepts.name: observational_learning
concepts.definition: Bandura 1977. Learning by watching others, without direct reinforcement. Bobo doll. Substrate analogue: in multi-substrate contexts, learning ActionSpecs by observing other substrate's successful dispatches.

concepts.name: vicarious_reinforcement
concepts.definition: Bandura. Observing other being reinforced for behaviour increases own likelihood of same behaviour. Substrate analogue: substrate's covers_correction update from observed peer-substrate outcomes.

concepts.name: modeling
concepts.definition: Bandura. Demonstrating target behaviour. Effective when model is similar + competent + rewarded. Substrate analogue: substrate's import of FilterSpec from peer substrate.

concepts.name: habituation
concepts.definition: Simplest learning: repeated exposure → reduced response. Found in all nervous systems. Substrate analogue: substrate's σ damping for repeatedly-encountered Concept without ΔF.

concepts.name: sensitisation
concepts.definition: Repeated exposure → increased response. Often follows aversive stimulus. Substrate analogue: substrate's amplified ΔF response after negative event.

concepts.name: preparedness
concepts.definition: Seligman 1971. Easier to condition biologically-prepared associations (taste-illness) than arbitrary ones. Substrate analogue: substrate's seed-Mt structure biases what associations form easily.

rules.name: rescorla_wagner_governs_associative_learning
rules.head: two concepts co-occur in the substrate
rules.body: their association strength updates proportional to prediction error (Rescorla + Wagner 1972). ΔV = α(λ - V) is exactly substrate's J update.

rules.name: extinction_is_inhibition_not_erasure
rules.head: the substrate stops reinforcing an ActionSpec
rules.body: the original learning persists; new inhibitory learning competes with it. Spontaneous recovery in different context. Substrate's covers_correction doesn't actually go to zero.

rules.name: blocking_prevents_redundant_learning
rules.head: an existing FilterSpec already covers a failure mode
rules.body: a new FilterSpec paired with the same mode doesn't acquire coverage — Kamin 1969. Substrate's derivation_mechanism + python_migration produce one tag per failure mode.

rules.name: variable_ratio_schedules_produce_persistent_behaviour
rules.head: the substrate's ActionSpec is reinforced unpredictably
rules.body: dispatch becomes highly persistent — extinguishes slowly. Why gambling + many habits are sticky. Substrate's coverage_count metric ≠ recent_success_rate.

rules.name: observational_learning_transfers_actions_across_substrates
rules.head: one substrate observes another's successful ActionSpec dispatch
rules.body: it can acquire the ActionSpec without direct trial. Bandura 1977. In collaborative contexts, FilterSpec/ActionSpec import.

rules.name: preparedness_biases_which_associations_form
rules.head: the substrate's foundational Mts include some seed concepts
rules.body: associations consistent with seed structure form faster than arbitrary associations. Seligman 1971. Substrate's seed bias.
